title.narrative: UNDP RCC Regional Elections Project Phase II 2017-2020
UNDP RCC Regional Elections Project Phase II 2017-2020

description.narrative: The Arab region continues to go through a period of change that is marked by some positive developments including a renewed drive for reforms, one of which is the return to the ballot box in key countries recovering from the consequences of the Arab spring. More governments are realizing the need for strengthening electoral systems and the ramifications that will follow a potential disregard of public demands for reform. Electoral processes remain at the essence of any democratic shift where societal changes will be part of the political agenda in any transitioning system. This intervention Regional Electoral Support Phase II 2017-2021 builds on Phase I (2014-2016) supported by Sida previously. UNDP, through this contribution, works with all concerned authorities that manage elections in the region as well as civil society, media, League of Arab States and other national and international stakeholders during 2017-2021 to implement this project. The overall goal of the intervention is to build and expand on the achievements of Phase I with the overall aim to improve accountability, participation and representation. The Global Project for Electoral Cycle Support (GPECS) Regional Component Phase II aims to contribute towards enhancing knowledge, awareness and capacity on electoral processes and regional cooperation among electoral stakeholders. The project constitutes of four main outcome objectives to be achieved by the end of the project: 1. Regional electoral capacity and knowledge enhanced; 2. Profession of electoral administration strengthened through regional cooperation; 3. Civic and political participation of women enhanced; 4. Role of youth in the electoral cycle promoted.
Democratic governance project, expanding on results achieved through electoral assistance support in MENA during Phase I.

UNDP har inkommit till Sida med förslag om stöd uppgående till totalt 65,8 MSEK för ett regionalt valcykelstödsprojekt för Mellanöstern och Nordafrika fas II för perioden 2017-2020. MENA-regionen kännetecknas ofta av bristande demokrati och lågt politiskt deltagande, särskilt bland ungdomar och kvinnor som utgör en utmaning för regionen. Det finns ofta behov av i MENA-regionen ökad kunskap om övergången till demokrati och internationellt accepterade valpraxis. Det övergripande målet och de förväntade effekterna av projektet är: "Medborgarnas förväntningar på röst, utveckling, rättsstatsprincipen och ansvarsutkrävande möts av starkare system för demokratiskt styre".
Insatsen har fyra resultatmål som ska uppnås i slutet av insatsen: 1) Stärkt regional valkapacitet och kunskap, 2) Stärkt professionalism inom valkommissioner genom regionalt samarbete, 3) Ökat kvinnligt deltagande i politiskt beslutsfattande och processer och 4) Främjande av ungdomars roll i hela valrörelsen. Målen förväntas uppnås genom b.la. utbildningsaktiviteter, seminarier, Syd-Syd samarbete, partnerskap med regionala nätverk inom media, partnerskap med andra regionala organisationer och samråd i valfrågor med landspecifika valmyndigheter.
Insatsen innebär i hög grad erfarenhetsutbyte och utbildningsaktiviteter. Ingen vidareförmedling kommer ske till nationella projekt eller partners. Projektet utgör en komponent av ett globalt projekt för valcykelstöd, Global Project for Electoral Cycle Support (GPECS). GPECS får stöd av Sida inom ramen för stöd från multilateralt samarbete. För denna insats är Sida ensam givare. UNDP kommer inte heller ge något direktstöd till den regionala organisationen för valkommissioner (Organization for Arab Electoral Management Bodies, ArabEMBs) utan ges i form av tekniskt stöd.
Sida finansierade den första fasen av programmet (2013-2016) och bedömningen är att resultaten av programmet var goda. Programmet utvärderades 2015 med slutsatsen att projektet på ett övertygande och konsekvent sätt hade uppnått målen. Projektet bedömdes ha skapat ett nära samarbete med Arabförbundet (Leage of Arab States) och stärkt dess kompetens och resurser för valfrågor. Det viktigaste resultatet bedöms vara etablerande av en regional organisation för valkommissioner. Projektet bedöms ha bidragit till ökad kunskap om valrelaterade frågor genom erfarenhetsutbyte och kapacitetsutveckling.

The Regional Electoral Support Project for the Middle East and North Africa (20172024) achieved noticeable progress in strengthening electoral governance, institutional cooperation, and inclusive participation across the Arab region. Next is Sida's assessment of the most important results:
- The project played a significant role in advancing the institutional development of ArabEMBs, which evolved from a small group of six founding members into a fully operational and regionally recognized organization with twelve members. With strengthened governance structures, an active secretariat, and regular regional assemblies and conferences, ArabEMBs became a hub for electoral cooperation, peer learning, and international engagement. It established partnerships with institutions such as the Venice Commission, IFES, International IDEA, and UN Women, and led regional observation missions that expanded professional experience among member EMBs. ArabEMBs continues to work toward long-term sustainability, supported by the projects efforts to guide financial planning, build partnerships, and strengthen internal governance.
- At the League of Arab States (LAS), the project significantly enhanced the capacity of the Electoral Affairs Department, transforming it into a more proactive regional convener and knowledge producer. LAS institutionalized regular data collection, analysis, and reporting on electoral processes across member states, producing more actionable and comparative insights. The project also helped LAS integrate gender-sensitive electoral training into its core capacity building programs, marking a major shift in an institution where gender had previously been excluded from electoral discussions. BRIDGE training became the primary methodology for LAS learning programs, with hundreds of practitioners benefiting. LAS further strengthened its role as a facilitator of regional collaboration by organizing thematic workshops, largescale electoral forums, and tailored trainings for its diplomats and electoral observers.
- The project contributed to embedding human rights principles in electoral processes through its work with the Arab Network for National Human Rights Institutions (ANNHRI). By providing technical support, tools, and platforms for engagement, the project enabled NHRIs to take on a more active role in electoral oversight, develop human rightsbased monitoring approaches, and collaborate more closely with EMBs. It also encouraged NHRIs to integrate gender sensitive perspectives, including monitoring violence against women in elections as a key human rights concern.
- Advancing women's electoral participation emerged as one of the projects most transformative achievements. The establishment of the Arab Network for Women in Elections (ANWE) created the first regional platform dedicated to promoting women's electoral rights, supporting reforms within EMBs, and shaping national awareness campaigns such as Her Participation, Our Future. EMBs across the region adopted gender action plans, developed internal gender policies, and began producing gender disaggregated electoral data. The project deployed e-Monitor in several countries to detect online misinformation, disinformation, and violence against women in elections, helping inform policy responses. Additionally, the creation of the Arab Women's Leadership Academy for the Digital Era strengthened women's leadership capacity and equipped them to navigate modern electoral challenges.
- Youth participation was strengthened through the projects strategic engagement with the UNDP Youth Leadership Programme (YLP). By connecting youth leaders with electoral institutions, the project helped shift youth inclusion from a marginal topic to a core regional priority. These efforts culminated in the establishment of the Arab Youth Network for Elections, now an active platform leading civic engagement initiatives, peer education, and youth driven collaboration with EMBs. The Network developed its own civic participation curriculum, contributing to long-term sustainability.
- The project also succeeded in fostering cross-sectoral cooperation between EMBs, CSOs, women's organizations, youth groups, and human rights institutions. It helped create joint initiatives, shared commitments, and inclusive action plans addressing gender equality, youth engagement, and human rights-based electoral administration. In response to emerging digital risks, the project mainstreamed discussions on information integrity, helping electoral institutions recognize the importance of digital preparedness and the threats posed by misinformation, disinformation, and online violence.
- The projects regional initiatives translated into direct national level impacts, supported by UNDP country offices and UN missions. National electoral actors adopted lessons from regional exchanges, strengthened strategic planning, integrated gender and youth considerations, and improved data practices. Participation in regional observation missions and thematic trainings exposed EMBs to diverse electoral models and encouraged adoption of regional best practices. Through these integrated efforts, the project contributed to creating a more professional, connected, and resilient electoral community across the Arab region and laid a foundation for sustainable, inclusive, and credible electoral processes in the years ahead.
